summary: In Greek mythology, Epistrophus (Ancient Greek: Ἐπίστροφος) was a Trojan ally who, with Odius, led the Halizones from Alybe "where silver is born" in Homer's Catalogue of Ships — a namesake of the Phocian captain son of Iphitus and of the warrior Achilles slew at Lyrnessus.

sections.heading: Halizone captain
paragraphs: Homer's Trojan Catalogue sets Epistrophus beside Odius at the head of the Halizones, who came from afar, from Alybe, where the birth of silver is. The pair stands among the Anatolian allies mustered for Priam; the poem does not narrate Epistrophus' later fate in the fighting.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: This atlas entry (epistrophus-halizone) is the Halizone co-captain with Odius. Distinct from Epistrophus son of Iphitus, the Phocian Achaean leader and Helen-suitor (epistrophus-phocis), and from Epistrophus son of Euenus, brother of Mynes, whom Achilles killed when he sacked Lyrnessus.
